Bachelor of Science with Honours in Applied Artificial Intelligence

This capstone project involves the research, design, and development of an open-source AI Red Teaming tool for assessing Large Language Model (LLM) and Generative AI applications against the OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 (2026) risk categories.
The tool will orchestrate existing open-source security testing frameworks (e.g. Garak,
, Inspect AI) alongside custom-built Python attack modules to execute security test cases, capture evidence, identify vulnerabilities, and generate reproducible,
The project addresses a capability gap within the Cyber Architecture & Development (CYAD) division: the ability to systematically red-team internally deployed GenAI applications
without relying on paid commercial tooling.
(Please use a separate sheet if necessary)
1. Research and document all ten OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 (2026) vulnerability categories and their applicable testing methodologies.
2. Evaluate existing open-source AI red-teaming tools (
, Garak, Giskard, Inspect AI) and recommend a technical foundation for the project.
3. Design and implement a modular tool architecture orchestrating open-source frameworks and custom attack modules.
4. Develop automated and semi-automated test modules covering all ten OWASP LLM Top 10 categories.
5. Build a finding-validation and evidence-capture engine that minimises false positives.
7. Benchmark the completed tool against existing frameworks and manual red-teaming for accuracy and coverage.

As organisations increasingly deploy LLM-powered applications for internal and public-facing use, the ability to systematically assess these systems against known AI-specific vulnerabilities is a growing operational necessity.

This project directly supports the Cyber Architecture & Development (CYAD) division's mandate to proactively secure AI systems, reducing reliance on costly commercial AI red-teaming products and building in-house capability aligned to an internationally recognised standard (OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026).

The project follows an approximately 32-week plan across eight phases:
Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4): Foundation & Research — AI Security Fundamentals Report; OWASP LLM Top 10 2026 Testing Matrix.
Phase 2 (Weeks 5-8): Open-Source Tool Evaluation — Tool Comparison Report; Tool Evaluation Report & Demonstration.
Phase 3 (Weeks 9-10): Tool Architecture Design — System Design Document.
Phase 4 (Weeks 11-16): Minimum Viable Product — Core Framework v0.1; LLM01 Attack Module; LLM02/LLM08 Modules.
Phase 5 (Weeks 17-24): Advanced Testing — RAG Security, Output Handling, Agentic Testing, remaining OWASP coverage.
Phase 6 (Weeks 25-28): Detection, Evidence & Reporting — Finding Validation Engine; Pentest Report Generator.
Phase 8 (Weeks 31-32): Finalisation — Tool Hardening; Final Presentation & Handover.
